title: Neal Hefti and Marshal Royal change the Basie sound; Nestico
summary: Edison says Hefti's voicings were a definite change, and he prefers Hefti to Sam Nestico's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, what I was going to say, after Basie had the small band and then he reformed and the band was not so different from what it had been, --
Right.
-- but then when Marshal Royal comes in and Neal Hefti does those arrangements, that's when it really changed, don't you think?
Yes, I think so. That was definitely -- that was a definite change in the Basie sound.
Yeah.

It really was. Well, Neal, he had his style of writing like Jimmy Mundy's, the guys that used to write for Basie, Eddie Durham's, you know, and Neal had a -- well, there was a different trend in writing with Neal and those guys, you know. Writing is just like playing, you know. You can get antiquated if you don't keep up, you know. And not that those guys didn't keep up with Neal -- he was the younger generation, you know. What he wrote was swing, but it was -- the voicing was altogether different.
Yeah, yeah.
Then I think he played quite a part in the resurgence of Basie's name.
Well, I mean, Joe Williams, too.
Well, that was before Joe, was before Joe.
Yes, that's right.
Basie made --
The atomic album (PHONETIC).
Yes, right. "Flight of the Fu-Fu Birds* ," and --
On Roulette. (R52003)
Yes. He had Snooky (Young) and he still had the band, but it wasn't making the noise until Joe Williams made "Every Day."

Yeah. But basically -- now you don't have to agree with me -- but it seems to me that what Neal Hefti did then, a combination of Neal and Marshal , now from that time on to today, they've -- that's really what it's been.
Oh, yeah.
I mean, he gets these arrangements by this guy (Sam) Nestico and they're like imitations of Hefti's.

Yeah. Well, Nestico, his arrangements don't -- Neal is the better of the two, you know. Nestico's arrangements sound like, to me, they have -- like a school, like the college kids' arrangements. You know? Basie likes that, but his arrangements really don't knock me out in Basie's band. I'd much rather have a Neal Hefti, even an old Neal Hefti arrangement, than a new Nestico arrangement.
